property_summary: A caller not approved by the owner can never successfully log an event.
A call to logCreated always returns true for any caller if and only if approvedToLog returns true for that same caller.
The return value of any logging function is exactly the return value of approvedToLog for the caller, and for a caller that is not approved, approvedToLog returns false.
A caller's approval status observed via any logging function is consistent with the public mapping of approvedLoggers for the same caller.
The return value of approvedToLog is equal to the stored approvedLoggers status for that address.

A caller can log if and only if it is approved; changing the approval check to always return the negation of a fixed unrelated address breaks the rule that a caller set as approved by the owner can successfully log.
The result of approvedToLog(x) must equal the stored approval status of x.
For any caller, approvedToLog returns the same boolean value as the corresponding entry in the approvedLoggers mapping, which the mutant always returns false for any caller that is in fact approved.
For any caller that the owner has approved via setApprovedLogger, approvedToLog must return true (the bug makes it always return false).

For every address and every approval status set by the owner, calling approvedToLog must return the same boolean value as the stored approvedLoggers mapping; the mutant breaks this by always returning false regardless of the mapping.

For any caller that has been approved by the owner (setApprovedLogger(caller, true) called by the owner), a subsequent call to approvedToLog(caller) must return true; the mutant always returns false, violating this rule.
For any address that has been explicitly approved by the owner via setApprovedLogger, approvedToLog must return true, but the mutant always returns false.
approvedToLog must return the approval status of the given caller, but the mutant always returns the status of address(0) regardless of the caller.

For any caller address, c.approvedToLog(caller) must return the value of approvedLoggers[caller]; the mutant always returns approvedLoggers[address(0)], which differs when approvedLoggers[caller] != approvedLoggers[address(0)].

For any caller address different from address(0), c.approvedToLog(caller) must return the approval status of the given caller; the mutant returns the status of address(0), violating the rule when the two statuses differ.

For any caller and any approval statuses, approvedToLog must return the actual approval status of the caller; the mutant always returns the status of address(0), which differs when the caller's status and address(0)'s status are set to opposite values.

For any caller address and any approval configuration, approvedToLog(caller) must return exactly the value of the public mapping approvedLoggers at that caller; the mutant returns approvedLoggers[address(0)] instead, so for any pair of callers where the two statuses differ, the outputs differ.
Only the owner can successfully toggle a logger's approved status.

property_summary: A non-owner caller cannot change the approved status of any logger; setApprovedLogger must revert.

For any call to setApprovedLogger, the mapping approvedLoggers must reflect the status for the _logger parameter, but the mutant always sets the status for address(0), so a non-zero _logger's approval remains unchanged when it should be updated.

After a non-zero-address caller with any status sets approvedLoggers via setApprovedLogger, a subsequent call to approvedToLog with that same caller address must return the status it was set to, but the mutant always sets address(0) instead, leaving the caller's approval unchanged.

After a non-owner calls setApprovedLogger with _logger != address(0) and _status == true, approvedToLog(_logger) returns true on the reference but false on the mutant because the mutant always sets address(0).

After owner sets approvedLoggers status for any logger address, approvedToLog for that same address must return the set status; the mutant always sets address(0), so for any non-zero logger the returned status stays false instead of the set value.

After the owner calls setApprovedLogger with any parameters, approvedToLog(address(0)) must return the _status value passed in that call, but the mutant incorrectly sets approvedLoggers for address(0) to _status even though the call was made with a different _logger, leaving address(0)'s approval unchanged from its prior state.

After any call to setApprovedLogger, the approvedLoggers status for the given logger must equal the _status argument; the buggy version always sets it to true, violating this equality when _status is false.
For any address a and caller c, if setApprovedLogger(a, false) is invoked by the contract owner, then approvedLoggers(a) must be false; the buggy version always sets it to true, violating this rule.
For any owner-pranked call to setApprovedLogger(logger, false), the logger's approvedLoggers status must be false; the buggy version always sets it to true, violating this when status is false.

For any two distinct addresses a and b, if the owner sets a's logger status to true and b's to false, then a must be approved and b must not be approved; the buggy version always sets both to true, so b will incorrectly appear approved.
After the owner calls setApprovedLogger for any address with _status=false, approvedLoggers for that address must be false; the bug always sets it to true.

After any call to setApprovedLogger, the caller's approval status equals the status argument passed to the function. The bug version ignores the argument, leaving the status unchanged, which breaks the rule for some inputs.

After any call to setApprovedLogger(logger, status), the logger's approval must match the status argument. The bug does not update the mapping, so approvedLoggers(logger) remains unchanged instead of matching status.
For any caller and logger, after a call to setApprovedLogger with status true, the logger's approval must eventually be true; the bug version does nothing, so the mapping never changes.

For any logger address and any boolean status, after an owner call to setApprovedLogger(logger, status) where owner is not the zero address, the approvedLoggers(logger) getter must equal status; the bug version leaves approvedLoggers unchanged, violating this rule for fresh loggers.

After an owner calls setApprovedLogger(logger, status), the public mapping approvedLoggers(logger) must return status; the bug version fails to update the mapping so the getter returns the previous value.
Only the contract owner can successfully change the approved logger status.

property_summary: A call to setApprovedLogger reverts for all callers that are not the owner, which is equivalent to: if the call succeeds, the caller must already be an approved logger or the status is set to false (since only the owner can add a new logger).
A non-owner caller cannot successfully execute any log function when only the owner is an approved logger.
A caller that is not an approved logger cannot cause a state change via setApprovedLogger, regardless of the caller's address, because only the contract owner can call it.
setApprovedLogger reverts unless called by the contract owner, regardless of the caller's approval status.
setApprovedLogger always reverts when called by any address other than the contract owner.
